title: Mounts
tagline: Every rideable creature and machine in Pywel — where it lives, how to make it yours, and what it is worth riding for.
asOf: Current to Charting the Unknown · November 2026

metrics.label: Speed
metrics.blurb: Top-end movement: the in-game Speed and Acceleration ratings for horses at max level, source descriptions for everything else.

metrics.label: Stamina
metrics.blurb: How long it can sprint, swim or fly before it slows: the in-game Stamina stat, or the use timer for timed mounts.

metrics.label: Travel
metrics.blurb: Total capacity to cover ground. Weighted mostly on speed, then stamina, then terrain traits — no fall damage, jumping, water sprint, flight — minus cooldown limits.

metrics.label: Combat
metrics.blurb: Mounted fighting value: Attack and Health, special attacks, and whether it keeps fighting after you dismount.

rules.text: A mount is ranked against others of its own class — Land, Sea or Sky — so a Tier I sea mount is the best thing that swims, not the best mount overall.
A mount with a decisive trait scores higher on the metric that trait serves: no fall damage lifts Travel, a unique attack lifts Combat.
They grow with riding and trust; beasts and machines arrive at full strength.
marks a metric that does not apply, such as Stamina on a balloon or mech.
Ratings are editorial calls built on recorded stats and the cited guides. Where no source compares a mount, it sits at Tier III and says so.

ladderNote: Tiers rank each mount against others of the same terrain. Ratings are editorial calls built on recorded stats and the cited guides.

leaves.label: Legendary
leaves.blurb: One of a kind: the three legendary horses, the sigil beasts, Blackstar, and the legends of the deep.
leaves.short: One of a kind — each exists once in Pywel.

leaves.blurb: Never sold at a stable — stolen, subdued, hatched or raised, then taken in for good.
